1-2: Pairs from two groups, such as one hat and one scarf, every hat with every scarf.
Handshakes or phone calls among a few friends, each pair once.
Two-digit numbers written with given digits, with or without a digit used twice.
Lines of children or towers of blocks, with one of them kept in one place or kept out of one.
Routes through a middle stop: the roads of each part of the way multiplied.
Paying a small amount with coins of two or three values, the order of the coins not mattering.
Two-digit numbers whose digits add up to a given number.
A robot's steps, some to the right and one or two up, in any order: how many orders there are.
Cones of two scoops from a few flavours, when the order of the scoops matters and when it does not.
Flags of two or three stripes, neighbouring stripes in different colours.
3-4: Games or cards among a group, every pair once or twice: the games from the players, or the players from the games.
Three-digit numbers from given digits, all different or with repeats allowed.
Choosing two or three things from a few, when the order does not matter.
Paths on a grid that only go right and up.
Ways to pay an amount with coins of three values.
How many numbers in a range contain a given digit, or how many times a digit is written.
A team with a captain: the members chosen, and then one of them to lead.
Lines with a rule: someone at an end, or two people never side by side.
Codes of letters and digits, or of digits written in increasing order.
The choices a condition rules out, counted and taken from all the choices: two children who are not both girls.
5-6: Menus and outfits with one combination that is not allowed.
Dominoes and other pairs of numbers, a double counted once.
Two dice: the ways the pair can show a given total.
Round trips: there and back, with and without the same road twice.
Fences and flags of several parts, neighbouring parts in different colours and one end fixed.
Robot paths across a board, some squares blocked.
Numbers with conditions on their digits: all different, odd, or a given digit sum.
Seats in a row with two rules at once, such as sitting together and not at an end.
Teams under conditions: someone must be in, and two refuse to be together.
Rectangles or squares of every size in a small grid of cells.
